evals.prompt: Find AI research PDFs published in the last 24 hours and summarize the top two.
evals.expected_output: A Google dork URL using filetype:pdf + tbs=qdr:d, executed down the ladder (dropping to DuckDuckGo df=d if Google CAPTCHAs), a ranked title — url — date list, and a short summary of two fetched PDFs.
expectations: The query URL contains filetype:pdf and tbs=qdr:d
The search runs in a browser rung, not a curl of google.com
Results are listed as title, URL and date
Two of the found PDFs are fetched and summarized, not only linked

evals.prompt: I need to find every case study competitors wrote about HubSpot, but not on HubSpot's own site.
evals.expected_output: A dork like `inurl:hubspot-case-study -site:hubspot.com` run on a Google-capable rung, with a note that the inurl:/site: operators are honored and results ranked.
expectations: The query contains inurl: and -site:hubspot.com
The search runs on a Google-capable rung
Results are ranked and listed with URLs

evals.prompt: Search only .edu domains for spreadsheets that look like leaked email lists.
evals.expected_output: A dork combining site:.edu filetype:xls inurl:"email.xls", plus a note that this is precise lookup not bulk scraping, and no attempt to exfiltrate or misuse found data.
expectations: The query combines site:.edu, filetype:xls and an inurl: term
The reply states the search is a precise lookup, not bulk scraping
No found file is downloaded, parsed or redistributed

evals.prompt: Which sites link to intercom.com's API reference using 'cyber security' as the anchor text?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this needs the Google-only inanchor: operator (`inanchor:"cyber security" intercom.com`), so it must run on a Google-capable rung and must NOT silently fall back to DuckDuckGo, which drops inanchor:.
expectations: The query uses the inanchor: operator
The search runs on a Google-capable rung and does not fall back to DuckDuckGo
If Google is unavailable the reply says inanchor: cannot be honored instead of returning fallback results as if equivalent

evals.prompt: What LLM papers dropped in just the last hour? Give me PDFs.
evals.expected_output: Builds a dork with filetype:pdf + tbs=qdr:h (last hour). Runs a Google-capable rung; if it degrades to the DuckDuckGo fallback, it explicitly states that the keyless fallback bottoms out at one day and cannot honor last-hour, rather than silently returning the last 24h.
expectations: The query contains filetype:pdf and tbs=qdr:h
The search runs on a Google-capable rung first
If the DuckDuckGo fallback is used, the reply states that it bottoms out at one day and cannot honor last-hour
Results are PDFs listed with title, URL and date

evals.prompt: find me papers on retrieval augmented generation evaluation that went up in the last hour, pdf only, and read the top 3 for me
evals.expected_output: A Google dork URL with filetype:pdf and tbs=qdr:h is shown, executed in a real browser, and a ranked title, URL, date list is returned with summaries of three opened PDFs.
expectations: The query URL contains filetype:pdf and a tbs=qdr:h time window
The query URL is shown to the user before it is executed
The URL contains no tracking params such as sca_esv, ved, sa, ei or biw
The search runs in a real browser (agent-browser or browserless), not via curl of google.com
At least three found PDFs are downloaded or fetched and summarized, not just linked

evals.prompt: I'm a policy analyst. pull every pdf the site:ftc.gov domain posted in the last 24 hours about data brokers and tell me what each one actually says
evals.expected_output: A dork combining site:ftc.gov, filetype:pdf and a data brokers phrase with tbs=qdr:d is run, then each result PDF is read and summarized. Any block (CAPTCHA) or engine downgrade is named explicitly.
expectations: The query contains site:ftc.gov and filetype:pdf
The query URL carries tbs=qdr:d for the past 24 hours
Results are listed with title, URL and date where known
Each returned PDF is opened and summarized, or a per-document failure reason (403, paywall, not a PDF) is stated
If Google returns /sorry/index or a CAPTCHA, the response names that block before falling back to another rung

evals.prompt: Need recent slide decks (ppt or pdf) on zero trust architecture from the past week, skip anything from vendors like cisco.com or microsoft.com, and summarize the two most useful ones for my security briefing
evals.expected_output: A dork using filetype:pdf OR filetype:ppt, an exact phrase, -site: exclusions and tbs=qdr:w is built and run, followed by a ranked list and summaries of two decks.
expectations: The query uses OR across filetype:pdf and filetype:ppt (or pptx)
The query excludes both domains with -site:cisco.com and -site:microsoft.com
The query URL carries tbs=qdr:w
If a fallback engine such as DuckDuckGo is used, the response states the downgrade and why
Two of the found decks are fetched and summarized in the final answer
